text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Austrian newspapers:
- The two petitions against gene-manipulation and for women's rights were a great success as more than 1.2 million Austrians signed the first and more than 600,000 signed the latter.
- The conservative People's Party's platform for open politics demands policy changes before the party is able to take on liberal-minded voters.
- Civil servants are harshly criticising Chancellor Viktor Klima's plan to continue austerity measures in public services, saying this move would be unethical for a Social Democrat.

- Iran and Iraq are surprised to hear of bugged hotel rooms in Vienna, however the U.S. secret service CIA's involvement in the case is only speculation, the interior ministry says, although it is certain a secret service was involved.
- Hannes Androsch's investment group won the bid for Austria's salt producer Salinen AG. The group will pay the 830 million schillings together with regional Raiffeisen Landesbank Oberoesterreich.
- 760,000 re-registrations are expected as prices for second hand cars tumble.
- 300 farmers in the north-east of Austria could lose up to 50 percent of their turnover should Unilever go ahead with the closure of its unprofitable subsidiary there.
- Shareholders are criticising a draft takeover law demanding small shareholders be treated equal.
- Klima's demand to reduce wages when work hours are reduced is meeting heavy resistance from within the party.
- Pressure from the European Union is pushing Transport Minister Caspar Einem to speed up the creation of a new telecommunications law.
- A new minimum corporate tax of five percent of the minimum share capital will be introduced retroactive to the beginning of the year.
- The metal worker's union, generally opposed to more flexible work hours, will give the industry a last chance to negotiate them.

- Austria's postal service sees a possibility to jointly bid with insurer Wiener Staedtische for the government's stake in postal savings bank PSK. Building society Wuestenrot wants to join the consortium of Bawag bank and insurer EA-Generali.
